pr_title: drivers: serial: nrfx_uarte: Add support to DMM  and data cache and other minor tweaks
pr_body:
Add support for DMM and cache.
Add configurable magic word used for RX flush workaround.
Add workaround for lack of retention of the BAUDRATE register in UARTE120.
Add lock to uart_rx_disable.

Fixes #77060.
pr_comments:
@anangl your comments applied.
@nika-nordic some comments applied. Due to resources usage I would stay with what we got regarding use of dmm where it is not needed.

After including dmm.h unconditionally `nrf52_bsim` target compilation started to fail due to lack of `soc/nordic/common` include path. I've added it to bsim boards. @aescolar can you take a look if that is ok?

issue_context.title: Race Condition in uarte_nrfx_rx_disable Function

review_comments: this could should compile fine for legacy targets as well - `dmm_buffer_in_prepare` is mocked for them: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/98e0e65069cf62297c4d03e0ad5b543374f5b735/soc/nordic/common/dmm.h#L134

im ifdefing because for dmm case there are additional fields in the data and config structure to hold user buffer (as it is different one than one used for DMA) and `mem_reg`. We could keep this for non-dmm cases and that would work but then its redundant so i preferred to ifdef it.

I guess this shouldn't be covered by `dmm`, as this is a case in which both `rx_flush_buf` and `buf` are located in cacheable RAM and in fact we are "emulating" DMA copying data from the former to the latter ?
but it is not , cache API is used. Commit states that DMM and cache support is added.
as above - this could should compile fine for legacy targets as well - `dmm_buffer_in_release` is mocked for them

`poll_in_byte` could be managed by `dmm` to avoid manual cache management in this case. `dmm_buffer_in_prepare` would need to be called before starting the receiver and `dm_buffer_in_release` on ENDRX. But again, this looks like special case as this single byte is used internally by shim while `dmm` was rather designed for user-provided buffers
yes, it would be much less efficient. Also for interrupt driven API this poll_in byte is used and if dmm would be used there then it would significantly impact the performance.

theoretically you could indiscriminately use `dmm_buffer_out_prepare` that would flush the cache for you and be transparent for the legacy targets. But I guess this could be purposefully omitted for performance reasons
there are several comments regarding indiscriminate usage of `dmm` APIs everywhere VS small potential savings in state variables. If you find them valuable they can stay, I guess
as above - `dmm` shouldn't be used here as this is a shim-specific code maintaining `rx_flush_buf` that happens to be located in cached RAM, right ?

as above - this could should compile fine for legacy targets as well - `dmm_buffer_in_prepare` is mocked for them: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/98e0e65069cf62297c4d03e0ad5b543374f5b735/soc/nordic/common/dmm.h#L134
